subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that the points whose position vectors are −2a + 3b + 5c, a + 2b + 3c and 7a − c are collinear, where a, b, c are non-coplanar vectors.

mark_split.label: Show PR is a multiple of PQ

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.61, chapter 6 ADDITION OF VECTORS, Very Short Answer question 13. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 shape is the one this bank uses for a Maths-1A Section A question: the first mark is for building PQ and PR from the position vectors, the second for showing one is a multiple of the other and naming the point they share. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty — Addition of Vectors has long been examined, we simply have no sourced years for this question. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The result was checked a second way with the third pair: QR = OR − OQ = 6a − 2b − 4c = 2 PQ, and PQ + QR = 3 PQ = PR, which is consistent.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show three points are collinear from their position vectors.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find PQ and PR
steps.margin_note: First mark. Name the points P, Q, R and take O as the origin. Because a, b and c are non-coplanar, their coefficients are collected separately, exactly as with i, j and k.
steps.memory_tip: Non-coplanar a, b, c behave like i, j and k: collect the a, b and c coefficients separately.
lines: Let P, Q, R be the points, with O as origin:

recall.must_convey: That PQ = OQ − OP = 3a − b − 2c and PR = OR − OP = 9a − 3b − 6c.
accept: subtract OP from OQ and from OR to get PQ and PR
PQ is three a minus b minus two c and PR is nine a minus three b minus six c
build two vectors from the same point P
OP ni theesi PQ, PR calculate cheyyali
take the differences of the position vectors from P
heard_as: three a minus b minus two c
nine a minus three b minus six c

steps.why: Non-coplanar means no one of a, b, c can be built from the other two, so the coefficients can be collected separately. It also guarantees 3a − b − 2c is not the zero vector, so P and Q are genuinely different points.
common_mistakes: Adding the position vectors instead of subtracting them.
Forgetting that OR has no b term, so its b coefficient is 0.
Building PQ and QR from different starting points and then comparing them.

steps.label: Show PR is a multiple of PQ
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Take the common factor 3 out of PR. Two vectors that are multiples of each other and start from the same point P must lie along one straight line.
steps.memory_tip: Take out the common factor: PR = 3 PQ. Multiple of each other plus a shared point P means one straight line.
lines: So PR and PQ are parallel, and P lies on both.

recall.must_convey: That PR = 3 PQ, and that with the common point P this makes the three points collinear.
accept: PR is three times PQ so they are parallel and share P, hence collinear
take three out of PR to get three times PQ
one is a scalar multiple of the other and P is common to both
PR equals three PQ, P common kabatti collinear
since PR is a multiple of PQ the three points lie on one line

steps.why: Vectors that are multiples of each other are only parallel on their own. It is the shared starting point P that forces the three points onto one straight line rather than onto two parallel ones.
common_mistakes: Stopping at PR = 3 PQ without saying that P is common to both.
Reading parallel as meaning the points cannot be collinear.
